Catch the Error, Warning or Message of an Instruction

Source: R/get_message.R
get_message.Rd

Evaluates an instruction written as a character string, and returns its error message, its last warning message or its standard messages (neither errors nor warnings), as a single character string.

Usage

get_message(
  data,
  kind = "error",
  header = TRUE,
  print_no = FALSE,
  text = NULL,
  env = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

data

Single character string: the instruction to evaluate.

kind

Single character string: the kind of message returned, either "error" (default), "warning" or "message" (standard messages).

header

Single logical value. Start the returned message with a header ("ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED:", "WARNING MESSAGE REPORTED:" or "STANDARD MESSAGE REPORTED:")? If FALSE, errors and warnings are returned as formatted by R (e.g., "simpleWarning in log(-1): NaNs produced" instead of "In log(-1): NaNs produced").

print_no

Single logical value. If TRUE, a "NO ... REPORTED" string is returned instead of NULL when nothing is caught (see the returned value).

text

Single character string inserted at the end of the header, before the colon (e.g., "ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED IN A:" with text = "IN A"), and added to the "NO ... REPORTED" strings whatever header. NULL (default) for no text.

env

Environment in which the instruction is evaluated (e.g., .GlobalEnv or asNamespace("stats")). If NULL (default), the environment from which get_message() is called.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

A single character string: the error message (kind = "error"), the last warning message (kind = "warning"), or all the standard messages, separated by line breaks (kind = "message").

If no such message is caught: NULL or, with print_no = TRUE, "NO (ERROR|WARNING|STANDARD) MESSAGE REPORTED". If the instruction stops with an error while kind is "warning" or "message", the warnings and messages emitted before the error are not returned: NULL or, with print_no = TRUE, "NO POTENTIAL (WARNING|STANDARD) MESSAGE BECAUSE OF ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED".

Details

The instruction is evaluated once, whatever kind. Its warnings and standard messages are caught and not displayed. Its printed outputs (e.g., by print() or show()) are not caught: use printed <- utils::capture.output(msg <- get_message(data = "print(1) ; log(-1)", kind = "warning")) to get them in printed. Text written directly to the standard error (e.g., by cat(file = stderr())) is not caught either: use utils::capture.output(type = "message") to get it.

Plots are drawn on a NULL pdf device (no file created), and the graphic devices left open by the instruction are closed. A ggplot2 object returned by the instruction is printed, to catch the errors, warnings and messages emitted when the plot is built.

See also

try.

Author

Gael Millot

Haiding Wang

Yushi Han

Examples

# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/get_message.html

# Error message returned by default. Here no error to report:
saferDev::get_message(data = "base::log(-1)", kind = "error", header = TRUE, print_no = FALSE,
    text = NULL, env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> NULL

# Warning message to report:
saferDev::get_message(data = "base::log(-1)", kind = "warning", header = TRUE, print_no = FALSE,
    text = NULL, env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "WARNING MESSAGE REPORTED:\nIn base::log(-1): NaNs produced\n"

# No standard message to report:
saferDev::get_message(data = "base::log(-1)", kind = "message", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "NO STANDARD MESSAGE REPORTED IN A"

# No standard message returned, because wilcox.test() stops with an error:
saferDev::get_message(data = "wilcox.test()", kind = "message", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "NO POTENTIAL STANDARD MESSAGE BECAUSE OF ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED IN A"

# Error message to report, with text added:
saferDev::get_message(data = "wilcox.test()", kind = "error", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED IN A:\nIn wilcox.test.default() : argument \"x\" is missing, with no default\n"

# No error message to report, with text added:
saferDev::get_message(data = "sum(1)", kind = "error", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "NO ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED IN A"

# A standard message is not reported with kind = "error":
saferDev::get_message(data = "message('ahah')", kind = "error", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "NO ERROR MESSAGE REPORTED IN A"

# Standard message to report, with text added:
saferDev::get_message(data = "message('ahah')", kind = "message", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE,
    text = "IN A", env = NULL, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> [1] "STANDARD MESSAGE REPORTED IN A:\nahah"

# Messages of a ggplot2 plot caught:
if(base::requireNamespace(package = "ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)){
    saferDev::get_message(data = "ggplot2::ggplot(data = data.frame(X = 1:10,
        stringsAsFactors = TRUE), mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = X)) + ggplot2::geom_histogram()",
        kind = "message", header = TRUE, print_no = TRUE, text = "IN INSTRUCTION 1", env = NULL,
        safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
}
#> [1] "STANDARD MESSAGE REPORTED IN INSTRUCTION 1:\n\033[1m\033[22m`stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`."
